shots.vo: What if tomorrow, instead of water, the sky poured *soda*?
Kids run outside with their mouths open. *Sweet!*
But soda is acidic: a pH of about *two and a half*. That's thirty times more acidic than acid rain.
Eyes sting. *Everyone runs* back inside.
A normal rain drops about *two gallons* on every square yard.
Soda has about a hundred grams of sugar per liter. So every square yard gets *two pounds of sugar*.
The asphalt turns sticky. *Shoes stick* to the road.
The sugar brings *wasps, bees and ants*.
Windows, cars, power lines — everything is covered in syrup. *Going outside* is scary.
The sugar washes into rivers. Bacteria feast on it and use up *all the oxygen* in the water.
It has happened before: in twenty thirteen, *fourteen hundred tons* of molasses leaked into Honolulu Harbor.
More than *twenty-six thousand* fish suffocated.
Now imagine every river and lake. The tap runs *cloudy, sweet water*.
In the fields, microbes feed on the sugar and take the nitrogen. *Nothing is left for the plants*.
The wheat turns yellow. A farmer looks at the field that fed his family *for a hundred years*.
Food prices soar. The most valuable thing on Earth is *plain clean water*.
The acid eats stone. Marble statues and cathedrals *lose their faces*.
Like the gargoyles of Notre-Dame from acid rain — only *many times faster*.
Kids born under the sweet rain have *never seen* a normal one.
So next time you get caught in the rain, smile. *It's just water*.
Would *you* go out in this rain?
